sixtySeconds.whatItDoes: Stable Diffusion web UI is a browser interface for generating images with Stable Diffusion on your own computer. It covers text-to-image and image-to-image, inpainting, outpainting, upscaling, LoRAs and embeddings, and a long list of extras, all through a Gradio web page.
sixtySeconds.problem: Running Stable Diffusion from scripts is fiddly. This web UI wraps it in a feature-rich interface with a one-click install and run script, so you can generate and refine images without writing code.
whoFor: Artists and hobbyists generating AI images
Users who want a classic, feature-rich Stable Diffusion UI
People with modest GPUs (4 GB, reportedly 2 GB)
sixtySeconds.whyChoose: Choose it for a mature, well-known interface with a huge feature set and extensions. Note it needs Python 3.10.6 on Windows, because newer Python versions don't support its torch version.
requirements: An NVIDIA GPU is recommended; AMD, Intel and Apple Silicon have guides
4 GB of VRAM (reports of 2 GB working)

overview: The web UI offers txt2img and img2img, inpainting and outpainting, prompt attention syntax, negative prompts, styles, variations, X/Y/Z plots, Highres Fix and a checkpoint merger. The Extras tab adds face restoration (GFPGAN, CodeFormer) and upscalers like RealESRGAN and SwinIR.

It supports textual inversion embeddings, hypernetworks and LoRAs, with a training tab. Generation parameters are saved inside each image, so you can drag an image to the PNG info tab to restore them. Custom scripts and community extensions add more, and there's an API.
Installation uses a one-click script, but you still need Python and git. On Windows with an NVIDIA GPU you can use the sd.webui.zip release package instead. The project is AGPL-3.0 licensed.
limitations: Apple Silicon, AMD and Intel setup lives on the wiki

install.verificationNote: Commands come from Stable Diffusion web UI's README. AIRepoHub hasn't run them yet.

steps.title: Download sd.webui.zip
steps.body: From the v1.0.0-pre release, then extract it.

steps.title: Install Python 3.10.6 and git
steps.body: Tick Add Python to PATH. Newer Python versions don't support torch here.

steps.title: Start it
steps.body: Run webui-user.bat from Windows Explorer as a normal, non-administrator user.

steps.title: Install dependencies (Debian-based)
steps.body: The README also lists Red Hat, openSUSE and Arch commands.
steps.code: sudo apt install wget git python3 python3-venv libgl1 libglib2.0-0

steps.title: Follow the Apple Silicon guide
steps.body: Instructions are on the project wiki's Installation on Apple Silicon page.

environment.name: python_cmd
environment.description: Set in webui-user.sh (for example python3.11) on systems where the default Python is too new.

tutorial.title: Generate your first image
tutorial.useCase: Install on Linux and create an image from a prompt.

steps.title: Write a prompt
steps.body: In the txt2img tab, enter a prompt and a negative prompt, then click Generate.

steps.title: Refine it
steps.body: Use emphasis like (tuxedo:1.21), try Highres Fix, or send the image to img2img.

tutorial.expected: The web UI opens in your browser and generates images, saving the generation parameters inside each image.

troubleshooting.problem: Install fails on a very new Linux
troubleshooting.solution: Install Python 3.11 or 3.10 and set python_cmd in webui-user.sh.
Use Python 3.10.6; newer versions don't support its torch.
Add --xformers to the command line arguments.
Follow the AMD or Intel installation guides on the wiki.
